graphEvents.label: OpenGhost and openhuman memory and skill stores
OpenGhost memory is one flat list with four hard limits

label: OpenGhost keeps one shared memory as a flat list with hard limits: 400 chars per record, 60 records, crowded at 28 records or 3600 chars.
Each OpenGhost record is id, text, at and by (agent or user): provenance is a two-value field, not a review state.
OpenGhost splits per-chat from shared: the chat record is a private file per chat, the memory is shared by all chats.
Extraction is a separate model call after each reply because the working model lets facts pass by.
The extractor writes a changed fact as an edit so no two lines disagree, and prefers the per-chat record when unsure.
Compaction is a model rewrite of the whole memory, not a delete.
A tidy result is accepted only when non-empty, strictly shorter, memory still on, and every source record still present.
OpenGhost skills are the open Agent Skills format: a folder with SKILL.md, a YAML head, then instructions, with side files read only when pointed at.
Skill discovery reuses ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills and the project equivalents, with the project winning on a name clash.
A skill is invoked as /name and its instructions reach the model wrapped in a skill_content element.
openhuman is a full memory subsystem: vendored TinyMemory engine, turn hooks, job queue, shared document brain, source registry, consent-gated backfill and one memory tool.
openhuman's per-agent split is configuration: identity_pins maps each agent to agent_id, root and recall.
openhuman's memory tool is budgeted and fails open: a refusal carries memory_budget metadata and the run continues without memory.
Licences split the reuse surface: OpenBot, OpenGhost and hermes-muse are MIT; openhuman is GPL-3.0; OpenMausBot, rakazo, turnstone and buzz are Apache-2.0.

reason: A vendored engine with a job queue, document brain and source registry, under GPL-3.0: wrong size and wrong licence for a small team.

direction: Treating OpenGhost's by field as a review gate
reason: An agent-written record is live at once; the user's control is edit and remove, not approve.
